dct_description_sm: This research project is a novel approach to investigate impacts of short-term environmental variations on subsistence economies.  The study is focused on archaeological middens at the Labrador Inuit site of Oakes Bay 1 (HeCg-08), occupied during the Little Ice Age.  Previous zooarchaeological studies at the study site designated a seal hunting subsistence economy that was largely consistent over time and that was especially dependent on hunting adult ringed seals (P. hispida). These results suggest that the impacts of climatic variability on Inuit subsistence in the Nain region were relatively limited or/and that the Inuit, through their mobility, technology and ecological knowledge, were able to cope with these events without wholesale changes in their hunting practices.  However, these studies rely on coarse stratigraphic sub-sampling of middens that obscure individual midden deposits indicative of short-term occupations. They do not profit from the possibility for a higher degree of chronological resolution offered by complex fine-scale midden stratigraphy.  The aim of this research is to combine zooarchaeological analyses of Oakes Bay 1 with high resolution micromorphological analyses of midden stratigraphy to better understand the evolution of subsistence economy represented by the site occupation.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Archaeology
dct_title_s: Zooarchaeological and micromorphological Data of Inuit archaeological site in Labrador
